newsitem.title: CANADA: Cominco sees stronger zinc prices in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Cominco sees stronger zinc prices in 1997.

text.p: Cominco Ltd, the world's biggest zinc miner, said Monday it expects stronger prices for the metal in 1997 although the market is still burdened by high stocks.
"We think this year will be better than last year, but the problem is inventories are still too high," Cominco chief executive officer David Thompson said in an interview.

He said zinc inventories were about 180,000 tonnes above normal "but moving steadily down toward normalization." Speaking at a mining conference, Thompson said western world zinc demand was projected to grow three percent this year.
"We expect western world refined zinc inventories to close 1997 at equal to or below normal levels," he said.

Thompson said world zinc prices had been too low to support investment in new zinc projects and that Cominco's Red Dog mine in Alaska was the only existing zinc mine with significant potential for expansion. Red Dog is slated to expand production by 40 percent in 1998.
Zinc reserves at producing mines of about 74 million tonnes would last for 14 years at 1995 production rates, Thompson said. This was only half as long as current copper reserves would last.
Moreover, several of the top 10 zinc mines will close or reduce production by 2005, Thompson said.
Cominco is actively seeking new deposits, targetting North and South America. "We are in the market for exploration deals," he said.
Cominco aims to expand its zinc production by about 250,000 tonnes by 2000, Thompson said. The company produced about 550,000 tonnes in 1996.
